title.narrative: Sierra Leone post landslide burial management

description.narrative:
Heavy rains in Freetown on the 14th August 2017 have caused a mud/landslide in Regent, Western Rural district and, a suburb of Freetown. It is estimated that up to 1,000 people have been killed. The city mortuaries were overwhelmed and the demand for burials outweighed capacity, unfortunately resulting in bodies left unburied. This is a huge health risk to the surviving population.
The Government of Sierra Leone recruited trained volunteers and staff to provide extra burial capacity. They approached CAFOD, CRS and WorldVision (as the SMART consortium responsible for Safe and Dignified burials during the ebola response) to support the cost of these activities.
This 3 week support will cover (some backdated) the weekly stipend of key burial workers including burial teams, decontamination teams, grave diggers etc. and fuel for vehicles. It will also be used to purchase key grave digging items such as markers and plaques. CAFOD's contribution will be earmarked to backdated salaries of gravediggers, burial volunteers (who started activities on 15 August 2017) and grave digging materials.
